## Simple Contagion

<div class="r-stack">

<div class='fragment'>
```{r, message=F}
create_notable('zachary') |>
  mutate(index = 1:nrow(.N())) |>
  mutate(infected = index %in% c(2,3)) |>
  ggraph() +
  geom_edge_fan(width = .1) + 
  geom_node_point(aes(color = infected), size = 3) +
  theme_graph()
```
</div>

<div class='fragment'>
```{r, message=F}
create_notable('zachary') |>
  mutate(index = 1:nrow(.N())) |>
  mutate(infected = index %in% c(2,3)) |>
  mutate(neigh_2 = index %in% neighbors(.G(), 2),
         neigh_3 = index %in% neighbors(.G(), 3)) |>
  mutate(infected = infected | neigh_2 | neigh_3) |>
  ggraph() +
  geom_edge_fan(width = .1) + 
  geom_node_point(aes(color = infected), size = 3) +
  theme_graph()
```
</div>

</div>


## Complex Contagion

<div class="r-stack">

<div class='fragment'>
```{r, message=F}
create_notable('zachary') |>
  mutate(index = 1:nrow(.N())) |>
  mutate(infected = index %in% c(2,3)) |>
  ggraph() +
  geom_edge_fan(width = .1) + 
  geom_node_point(aes(color = infected), size = 3) +
  theme_graph()
```
</div>

<div class='fragment'>
```{r, message=F}
create_notable('zachary') |>
  mutate(index = 1:nrow(.N())) |>
  mutate(infected = index %in% c(2,3)) |>
  mutate(neigh_2 = index %in% neighbors(.G(), 2),
         neigh_3 = index %in% neighbors(.G(), 3)) |>
  mutate(infected = infected | (neigh_2 & neigh_3)) |>
  ggraph() +
  geom_edge_fan(width = .1) + 
  geom_node_point(aes(color = infected), size = 3) +
  theme_graph()
```
</div>

</div>

## Discussion Questions

- How can we determine whether someone is actually influential or if they just happened to be in the right place at the right time when something became popular?
- Think about a time you started doing something new, like trying an app, a trend, or a habit. Did one person convince you, or did it take several friends doing it first? What does that say about whether it was a simple or complex contagion?

## Discussion Questions

- If the success of a trend depends more on the structure of social networks and the willingness of people to adopt it than on influential individuals, why do companies continue to invest so heavily in influencer marketing?
- In complex contagion, how can we distinguish the effects of reinforcement from multiple social contacts from other factors, such as tie strength or similarity between individuals? For example, if someone adopts a behavior after observing several friends doing it, how can we determine whether the adoption resulted from social reinforcement or from shared characteristics and preferences?
